## Motivation

The recent "Discrete Log, Weil, and Akiyama Conjectures Broken" paper is a good illustration of the kinds of work we expect our mathematical redundancy will produce. The problem, which was related to resource bounded Kolmogorov complexity, had existed since the 1970s, and had recently become moderately interesting again after Watanabe and Kawarabayashi had proven the real-valued analogues of the conjecture. The problem turned out to be difficult in practice. A professional mathematician and a former AI researcher published a 37-page set of results, including counterexamples to all three conjectures, after finding a 3-line counterexample by hand to one of the conjectures and iteratively generalizing this hand-generated counterexample to more general cases. The proofs were not straightforward, and relied on multiple tools. This work, because of the new techniques and general patterns it established, may be relevant to breaking other conjectures, and hints at a way to use or adapt these techniques to render known incomputability, undecidability, or NP-hardness results infeasible in practice.
